māyā: [Maya+ṇe+ā] (thī) CL=7 [Mayati vividhākāraṃ gacchati etāyāti māyā. Nirutti, nhā.557, maya+ṇa+ā. Mayena asurena sure vañcayituṃ payuttattā mayassa ayaṃ māyā. Dhāna,ṭī.512.mā+ya+ā. māḷa: [Mā+ala] (pu,na) CL=7 [ma+alaṃ.(ma2- See). Mā+ḷa. Māti gaṇhāti sampatta-sampattajanānaṃ cittanti māḷaṃ. Athavā(mānaṃ,)sampattayatigaṇānaṃ cittassa vivekakaraṇe alanti māḷaṃ. Apa,ḷa,2.176. Mānitabbo-ti māḷo,miyati pamiyatīti vā māḷo. Sī,ṭī,saca,1.198. Mā mone, ḷo. Dhāna, ṭī.209.] The meeting hall or conference building. The open pavilion. The circular shape pavilion.
māḷaka: [Māḷa+ka] (pu,na) CL=7 [Māḷa+ka. Māḷameva māḷakaṃ. Apa, ṭṭha,2.176.] The pavilion.
māḷakacchanna: [Māḷaka+channa] (pu) CL=7 The roof of a pavilion.
māḷakasīmā: [Māḷaka+sīmā] (thī) CL=7 The boundary of a small lodge. Khaṇḍasima.
māḷasaṅkhepa: [Māḷa+saṅkhepa] (pu) CL=7 The appearance or shape of the pavilion.
māṇava: [Manu+ṇa] (pu) CL=7 [Moga,4.8. Manu+ṇava. Rū,nhā.221. Dantajana- and Mānavasaddā explain the meaning of creatures or beings.  muddhajaṇa- and Māṇavasadda explain the meaning of a disgusted son or very foolish son. In Nīti,dhā.264-5, explains as Kecivāda. The son of a wholesome person named Mānava and that name is written with Na. The lazy person who is the son of a bad person, that son named Māṇava and that name is written with (Muddhajaṇa) Ṇa. In Prekana paccaññaḥ, Sya,2.348-sutta, it explains Sakkata kāsikāvutti, jinindabuddhinyāsa. In Rū,nhā.221, there is Dantaja Na and Mānava saddā. In Moga. Moga, pañcīkā,4.8, there is both Mānava and māṇavasaddā]. (1) (A) Beings or creatures. (B) People. (C) Human. (D) A man. (2) A thief. (3) A young man. A bachelor. (4) A person named Māṇava. See also - Māṇavatthera.
